title: A violent F5 tornado strikes around Brownwood, Texas, injuring 11 people. Two people were thrown at least 1,000 yards (910 m) by the tornado and survived uninjured.
text: During the evening hours of April 19, 1976, a violent tornado struck Brownwood, Texas, United States. The damage caused by the tornado was extreme enough for the National Weather Service to rate the tornado F5 on the Fujita scale.

title: The Great Bookie Robbery in Melbourne, Australia: Bandits steal A$1.4 million in bookmakers' settlements from Queen Street, Melbourne.
text: The Great Bookie robbery was a heist committed in Melbourne, Australia, on 21 April 1976.

title: Portugal's new constitution is enacted.
text: The Constitution of Portugal, officially the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic, is the supreme law of Portugal. Approved on 2 April 1976 and becoming effective on 25 April of the same year, it superseded the Estado Novo's 1933 Constitution after the Carnation Revolution.

title: Faber–Jackson relation presented by astronomers Sandra M. Faber and Robert Earl Jackson.
text: Sandra Moore Faber is an American astrophysicist known for her research on the evolution of galaxies. She is the University Professor emerita of Astronomy and Astrophysics at the University of California, Santa Cruz, and works at the Lick Observatory.

title: Gravity Probe A, a satellite-based experiment to test Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity, is launched.
text: Gravity Probe A was a space-based experiment to test the equivalence principle, a feature of Einstein's theory of relativity. It was performed jointly by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

title: Viking program: The Viking 1 lander successfully lands on Mars.
text: The Viking program consisted of a pair of identical American space probes, Viking 1 and Viking 2 both launched in 1975, and landed on Mars in 1976. The mission effort began in 1968 and was managed by the NASA Langley Research Center.

title: NASA releases the famous 'Face on Mars' photograph, taken by Viking 1
text: Cydonia is a region on the planet Mars that has attracted both scientific and popular interest. The name originally referred to the albedo feature (distinctively coloured area) that was visible from earthbound telescopes.

title: Luna program: Luna 24 successfully makes an unmanned landing on the Moon, the last for 37 years.
text: The Luna programme, sometimes called Lunik by western media, was a series of robotic spacecraft missions sent to the Moon by the Soviet Union between 1959 and 1976. The programme accomplished many firsts in space exploration, including first flyby of the Moon, first impact of the Moon and first photos of the far side of the Moon.

title: Space Shuttle Enterprise rolled out.
text: Space Shuttle Enterprise is the first orbiter of the Space Shuttle system. Rolled out on September 17, 1976, it was built for NASA as part of the Space Shuttle program to perform atmospheric test flights after being launched from a modified Boeing 747.

title: July–August – Articles by Geraldine Norman in The Times (London) expose a number of paintings attributed to Samuel Palmer as the work of Tom Keating, which he does not deny.
text: Samuel Palmer Hon.RE (27 January 1805 – 24 May 1881) was a British landscape painter, etcher and printmaker.

title: Completion of the Cubist-influenced Church of the Holy Trinity, Vienna, by Fritz Wotruba.
text: The Kirche Zur Heiligsten Dreifaltigkeit, better known as the Wotrubakirche or Wotruba Church, is a Catholic church located in Liesing, Vienna. It was built between August 1974 and October 1976, based on a design by Austrian sculptor Fritz Wotruba.

title: Collection de l'art brut ("Collection of outsider art") established in Lausanne, Switzerland.
text: The Collection de l'art brut is an art museum dedicated to outsider art located in Lausanne, Switzerland.
